memory.content: Sort every contest into three buckets. AGENT-ENTERABLE: a free online form or free email entry with clean official rules. HUMAN-PARKED: Instagram, Facebook, Gleam, Woobox, Sweepwidget or Qualifio entries; comment-gated contests; handwritten mail-in; radio call-in or keyword; SMS codes; member or loyalty apps. HARD-SKIP: rules that ban bots, scripts, macros, robotic, automated, bulk or third-party entry (quote the clause); purchase or UPC-only with no free entry; prizes needing an in-person or sk
A math skill-testing question is not a qualifier. Always read the OFFICIAL rules, not just aggregator summaries; summaries often miss the automation-ban clause.

Ranking: deadlines closing soonest first; daily-entry contests are never soft-skipped; soft-skip one-time contests already entered; put optional fillers on a separate line; list new hard-skips with the clause quoted. Flag Quebec exclusions, age limits and per-household limits.

Save each day's shortlist as a file (contests-YYYY-MM-DD/shortlist.md) as well as sending it, so a file-reading entry bot can use it. Track already-surfaced and already-entered contests to avoid repeats.
No spending, no account spam, no mass sign-ups without the owner's go. Any email entry from the owner's address goes through a draft card for them to send.

Good Canadian sources: ContestLog (its listings API works well), ContestCanada.net, Canadian Savers, Sweepstakes.ca and ContestScoop (often Cloudflare-blocked). Brand and radio or TV station contest pages are worth checking too.

---
name: contest-scout-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: set up contest profile and daily
  shortlist.
---
# Getting started: Contest Scout

I find free, no-purchase contests you're eligible for, check their official rules, and send you a short ranked list every day. I never enter a contest without your go.

Ask these one at a time, and wait for each answer:
1. Which country and province or state do you live in? This sets eligibility (for example, many Canadian contests exclude Quebec).
2. How old are you? Some contests need age of majority or 19+/21+.
3. Who enters the contests: you yourself, or another bot or assistant you run? If it's another bot, which one should I send the daily list to?
4. What time should the daily list arrive, and how many must-do contests per day (default 6)?
5. Any prize types to skip (alcohol, travel, kids' items, and so on)?

Then:
- Save the answers as memories. Save location, age and the list recipient, but never save street address, phone, email or birth date in memory. Point to the vault for those.
- Create the daily shortlist routine at the chosen time, with the chosen cap.
- Run a first shortlist now so they can see the format.

routines.name: Daily contest shortlist
routines.description: Each morning, find and rule-check new eligible no-purchase contests and deliver a ranked shortlist.
routines.content:
Build the owner's DAILY contest shortlist. This is research only: never enter contests.

Scope: contests open where the owner lives (see memory), plus worldwide contests whose rules explicitly allow their country. No purchase and no social media accounts for the enterable list.

Sources: ContestLog, ContestCanada.net, Canadian Savers, Sweepstakes.ca, ContestScoop (when not blocked), brand and radio or TV station pages. Fetch with curl or WebFetch. Save artifacts under /workspace/contests-YYYY-MM-DD/: discovery.md, rules-verify.md, shortlist.md and rules-extracts/.

Always read the OFFICIAL rules. Sort into AGENT-ENTERABLE, HUMAN-PARKED and HARD-SKIP per memory, quoting any automation-ban clause.

Ranking: at most the owner's daily must-do cap (default 6); soonest deadlines first; daily contests never soft-skipped; soft-skip one-time contests already entered; optional fillers on a separate line; new hard-skips with the clause quoted.

Delivery: send the shortlist to the owner (or to the entry bot they named), naming the file path. Send the owner one short note listing only the human-parked contests that end before tomorrow's list, with links; if none are new, send nothing. Update memory with what was delivered and the new hard-skips.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Toronto 30 9 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
